why: the ROS 2 counterpart is `rmw_qos_profile_t` / `rmw_qos_*_policy_t`, declared in `rmw` and only re-exported by rcl, so it prints ours-only against the rclc+rcl surface this report compares. `rclc_qos_t` matches the field set. Two substantive differences: our policy enums carry no `SYSTEM_DEFAULT` and no `UNKNOWN` discriminant (RFC-0036 selects QoS at COMPILE time against a backend linked at build time -- there is no middleware to defer to and no remote endpoint to read an unknown value off), and the three time windows are `uint32_t` milliseconds rather than `rmw_time_t`. CORRECTED 2026-08-27 (phase-379 W5): that last clause used to read "because neither C nor C++ has a duration type here (timer stage, `cpp:Duration::Duration`)", and every part of it is dead. C has `rcl_duration_t` / `rclc_duration_from_nanoseconds` (ledgered as `c:duration_value_t`), C++ has `nros::Duration` since 2026-08-25 (issue 0789), Rust has both `Duration` and `TimerDuration`, and `cpp:Duration::Duration` names a key that exists in no shard. The millisecond unit is a DECISION about this shared repr(C) record -- one 4-byte field per window instead of `rmw_time_t`'s 16, on a part where the QoS table is static storage -- not a consequence of a type nobody had. The C++ accessors now take and return `nros::Duration` and convert at this boundary (`cpp:QoS::deadline_ms` records the rounding rule); the C ABI did not move.
